record.context_brief: Independent sets above the planar n/4 threshold
record.original_question: Given an n-vertex planar graph G, can one find in polynomial time an independent set of size floor(n/4)+1, or alternatively prove that obtaining such a set is NP-hard?

evidence.quote: Question 5.2. For a given n-vertex planar graph G, is it possible to find in polynomial time (or to show that this is NP-hard) an independent set of size bn/4c + 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
By the Four Color Theorem, every planar graph on n vertices contains an independent set of size at least ⌈n/4⌉. The question concerns going one vertex above this guaranteed threshold.

Problem. Let G be a planar graph on n vertices. Decide which of the following holds:
(a) There exists a polynomial-time algorithm that, given any n-vertex planar graph G, outputs an independent set in G of size ⌊n/4⌋ + 1, or correctly reports that no such independent set exists.
(b) The decision problem "Does the given n-vertex planar graph G contain an independent set of size ⌊n/4⌋ + 1?" is NP-hard.

Determine whether (a) or (b) holds (or establish another rigorous classification of the complexity of finding an independent set of size ⌊n/4⌋ + 1 in an n-vertex planar graph).
artifact.status_search_result: General-search results discuss maximum independent set on planar graphs (NP-hard in general, with PTAS via Baker's technique) and the n/4 lower bound from the Four Color Theorem, but no source directly resolves the specific question of computing an independent set of size exactly ⌊n/4⌋+1 in polynomial time or proving NP-hardness of this exact threshold problem. The status appears to remain unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: The Maximum Independent Set Problem in Planar Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Maximum independent set on planar graphs is NP-hard in general; restricted classes admit polynomial algorithms.
status_evidence.claim: General hardness context for MaxIS on planar graphs, but does not address the n/4+1 threshold specifically.

status_evidence.title: An Approximation Algorithm for the Maximum Independent Set Problem on Planar Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: PTAS-style approximation algorithms exist for planar MaxIS.
status_evidence.claim: Approximation results exist but do not resolve the exact ⌊n/4⌋+1 threshold question.
